text.p: These are the main stories in the Latvian newspapers on Friday. Prepared for Reuters by the Co-operation Fund. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- Parliament confirmed New Minister of Finance, Roberts Zile, by 68 votes to 4.
- The minister of economics, Guntars Krasts, has ordered the suspension of a planned rise in electricity tariffs.

- 41 deputies backed the proposal of Ziedonis Chevers, the leader of Democratic Party Saimnieks, to set up a parliamentary committee to investigate into the misuse of G-24 credits and to establish the personal responsibility of those involved in squandering the credits. 38 MPs also signed a proposal to investigate a planned merger between Unibanka with Savings Bank.

- Russian Deputy Prime Minister Valery Serov met Prime Minister Andris Shkele and Foreign Minister Valdis Birkavs. The main topics were bilateral relations, economic co-operation and the need to conclude several interstate agreements.

- The two strategic investors of Latvia's gas company, the Russian gas concern Gazprom and the German consortium, including Preussen Elektra and Ruhrgas, are to buy $30 million worth of the company's shares by August 15, said the general director of the Latvian Privatisation Agency, Janis Naglis.
- The rate of discount of the Bank of Latvia will be cut to six percent from March 1.
- The internal debt was 190.536 million lats on February 26, which is 3.288 million less compared to a week ago. On February 26, the budget surplus was 7.771 million lats.
- Parliament has for the fourth time rejected the proposal of deputy Modris Lujans to re-establish March 8 as Latvia's Womens day.
- Daugavpils, Latvia's second largest city, is to establish closer economic links with Moscow by concluding an economic co-operation treaty with the Russian capital's central district.
